claims.statement: `mcp_server._effective_write_surface()` is the sole coercion of an operator's `--allowlist` into the effective write surface: `None` passes through as `None`, which is blocklist mode (the protected-path refusal plus governance fence are the only bound), while an explicit list narrows. The same value is consumed by the write tool's `allowlist=` and by `list_folders`' writability flag, so discovery cannot advertise a path that `commit_note` refuses.

`DEFAULT_WRITE_ALLOWLIST = (notes/, sources/, dashboards/, captures/)` is no longer the default write surface; it is retained only as a named opt-in escape hatch an operator can pass via `--allowlist` to restore the old note-zone-only surface.

A write-enabled serve is refused at construction for two misconfigurations: an explicit but effectively empty `--allowlist` (which would permit no writes at all) and a half-wired auth surface (AuthSettings plus token_verifier/auth_server_provider supplied inconsistently, or both verifiers), so no half-open server is ever built.

`serialize.protected_reason()` encodes protected classes as rules (not a fixed path list), refusing them unconditionally regardless of caller and independently of any allowlist, which is why the guard still holds when the engine is dropped into an arbitrary repo: protected directories (`.git`, `.github`, `.obsidian`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `views`, `scripts`, `bin`, `hooks`, `skills`, `.hypermnesic`), CI workflow dirs, git-hook installers, agent-instruction files anywhere including nested, and the never-write metadata files.

The governance fence refuses a code-exec/build/CI/credential file class positively by name and extension — `dockerfile`, `makefile`, `containerfile`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.env`/`.env.*`, and the `.yml`/`.yaml`/`.lock`/`.toml` extensions — matched case-insensitively and applied AFTER the directory checks so the more informative protected-dir reason wins (e.g. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` reports a protected dir).

Protected-directory matching is case-folded (`part.lower() in _PROTECTED_DIRS`), closing the case-insensitive-filesystem hole where `Scripts/evil.sh` lands in the protected `scripts/` directory on disk; the never-write files (`.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules`) deliberately remain case-sensitive, an accepted low-severity residual because they are not an execution or credential vector.

`serialize.writable_reason()` is the single source of truth for the is-this-writable decision — protected-class refusal first, then optional allowlist narrowing — returning the sentinel `_NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST` for an allowlist miss so the predicate stays path-clean; `check()` re-derives two distinct caller-facing messages from it (`refused protected path … : <reason>` versus `path … not in writable allowlist`).

`serialize.check()` enforces within-repo resolution before any file work: absolute paths are refused outright, the path is resolved against the resolved repo root and refused if the result escapes it (catching both `..` traversal and symlink escapes by real resolution), and the normalized repo-relative posix path is returned for the caller to write.

Folder discovery single-sources writability from the same guard by probing a synthetic `__probe__.md` under each folder prefix with `writable_reason`; because the probe is a note and compares a file under the prefix, a folder can be `writable: true` for notes while a governance file at the same level is still refused, and a nested protected directory such as `projects/scripts/` is correctly reported unwritable.

Owner-facing surfaces reuse the same guard rather than re-implementing it: `memory_control` derives each memory's `writable` flag and `protected_reason` from `serialize.writable_reason()` and answers write-scope questions through `folders.derive_folders()`, and the CLI `list-folders` preview reuses `mcp_server._effective_write_surface` so the preview cannot drift from the live write surface.

`serialize.FileLock` is an advisory exclusive `flock` that conflicts across descriptors even within one process, acquired non-blocking by default and raising `LockBusyError` rather than queueing — the property that makes it effective against a second in-process writer.

Two lock granularities exist: `index_write_lock()` (the single-indexer lock at `.hypermnesic/index.lock`, held by `commit_note`/`rename_note` around their locked section) and `path_lock()` (per-path, hash-keyed under `.hypermnesic/locks/`, so distinct paths proceed concurrently); the process-local lock gives no cross-process exclusion between committers — the path-scoped git add/commit pathspec is what isolates one writer's commit from another's staged work.

`serialize.preflight()` returns HEAD and raises `HeadDriftError` when HEAD moved from the base a caller read and `DirtyTreeError` for broad writers on an unclean tree; the engine's own `.hypermnesic/` state directory is ignored via `.git/info/exclude` (never by editing the vault's `.gitignore`), so it never registers as a dirty change.

`serialize.branch_commit_transaction()` lands a set of files as ONE atomic commit on a fresh branch inside an isolated temporary worktree, never touching the owner's live HEAD, and rolls back both the worktree and the half-built branch on any failure so no partial or orphan branch ref survives; callers gate each file's content before calling, so a gate abort never creates a branch.

`write_enabled ⇒ auth-required` is enforced at server construction on any non-loopback bind (refusing to start without a configured verifier, with the unconditional `0.0.0.0`/wildcard refusal firing first); a loopback bind is exempt because only the local user can reach it, and the `trust_tailnet_write` / `--allow-tailnet-write` opt-in relaxes the requirement ONLY for a literal Tailscale CGNAT bind (`100.64.0.0/10`), refusing any other non-loopback host with a distinct error.
`commit_note` is registered as an MCP tool only when the serve is built with `write_enabled=True`, so a read-only serve is structurally incapable of writing.

The `write` scope is enforced per-tool inside `commit_note` from `get_access_token()`, independent of the transport's global `required_scopes` (the SDK applies one scope list to all tools and so cannot separate read from write clients on a single endpoint): a token lacking `write` is refused with an `insufficient_scope` message that states write approval does not bypass the other guards, and nothing is written.

On the public lane, Dynamic Client Registration lets any internet client register, so `authorize()` never mints a code — it stashes the request and redirects to an operator-authenticated consent page, and only `finalize_consent()` with the operator approval token issues a code. The approval token is stored only as a hash and compared with `hmac.compare_digest`, and pendings are bounded by `PENDING_TTL_SECONDS` (600), `MAX_CONSENT_FAILURES` (5), `MAX_PENDING` (256), and `MIN_APPROVAL_TOKEN_LEN` (24).

The resource-server token verifier fails closed and enforces RFC 8707 audience binding plus expiry: any raw-validation exception, a `None` result, an expired token, or a token whose audience does not include this resource server (including a token with no audience at all) yields `None` and therefore a 401, and the token is never logged.

A refused write is never a silent success: `WriteGuardError`, `FrontmatterDriftError`, `HeadDriftError`, `DirtyTreeError`, `GitCoordinationError`, and input-shape `ValueError` are all mapped to `committed: false` with a `refused` reason instead of a raw traceback, and the audit entry is appended only after the write reached the shared remote, so no audit entry exists for a refused write.

The embedding credential is read from the environment or a gitignored `.env` (repo root first, then the working directory) only; a missing key raises `ConfigError` naming only the source categories checked, and `api_key_status()` exposes secret-free metadata (a configured flag, a source category, the categories checked) — never a filesystem path or a key value.

The audit log is append-only JSONL recording `{ts, actor, verb, path, old_sha, new_sha, summary}` with summaries only (never page bodies), truncated at `MAX_SUMMARY`; refusal entries additionally pass a token-shaped-string redaction; an append leaves prior lines byte-identical; the actor is server-set from the verified node identity with a fixed sentinel fallback and a caller-supplied actor is ignored; and a reconciler back-fills entries for commits that reached HEAD without being logged, so a crash between commit and append is recoverable.

Client-facing diagnostics never echo secret values: `local_proof` redacts bearer tokens, key-shaped strings, approval-token assignments, and operator home paths from anything it echoes, and `doctor` inspects the consent-secret file by existence and file mode only (passing only at owner-only permissions, otherwise warning with a chmod repair action) without reading its value.

Public-lane OAuth runtime state (registered clients, codes, access/refresh tokens, grants) is persisted to an owner-only `0600` file, `.hypermnesic/cloud-oauth-state.json`, written through a temp file plus `os.replace`, while the owner-facing grant store is a separate secret-free artifact: `client_control` persists only an allowlisted set of metadata keys and drops everything else, so grants can be listed and revoked without handling credentials.

Folder discovery sanitizes root-local instruction content before returning it to a remote client, replacing endpoint URLs and host-local absolute paths with `<endpoint-url>` and `<local-path>` placeholders so host coordinates never ship through a read tool.

`scripts/preflight_public_scan.py` is the enforced public-surface leak gate: it scans git-tracked files for operator-specific identifiers and credential material, masks every matched value before printing so the gate never re-prints a secret, exits non-zero on a hit, always excludes the launch-staging directory and its own script/test, defers inherited process-history docs in default mode (reporting the count) while `--strict` scans all of `docs/` and `--history` adds an informational commit-diff scan; CI runs the default gate alongside lint, tests, and the license scan.

`docs/threat-model-commit-note.md` is the threat model of record for the write surface (a signed-off living root document whose vectors map to the live modules and which carries dated topology amendments), and every later review is an immutable delta carrying `amends:`/`signed_off:` frontmatter, so the set forms an audit chain in which a new finding is a new dated review rather than an edit.

Frontmatter reserialization churn is treated as a data-integrity failure, not a formatting detail: the write computes the new text through a byte-preservation gate and aborts with the offending diff on any un-requested frontmatter change instead of writing.

The blocklist flip is enforced by a test gate, not convention: while `_effective_write_surface(None)` returns `None` (the blocklist default is live), the dated blocklist review delta must exist and carry a non-empty, non-`PENDING` `signed_off:` value, otherwise the test fails and blocks merge/enable of the flip.

The write-surface threat model groups the original vectors (protected-path escalation, prompt injection via ingested content, frontmatter clobbering, actor spoofing/repudiation, audit-log leak, path traversal, .gitignore side effects, concurrent-writer corruption, credential exposure, crash recovery) and the resource-server vectors added when auth moved into scope (token-validation bypass, audience/issuer confusion, AS compromise and availability blast radius, the inverted failure mode where an auth bug opens the write tool, and the bounded tailnet-trust write opt-in).

Prompt injection through retrieved content is bounded but explicitly NOT solved: the engine treats retrieved content as data rather than instructions, never auto-acts on it, and every write is an explicit authenticated call, and even a successful injection cannot reach the protected classes — but content is not sanitized for injection, so a downstream agent harness must treat retrieved content as untrusted (a stated integration assumption and accepted risk).

The accepted residuals of the current write model, each with a disposition, are: the widened blast radius of a consent-approved injected LLM (accepted as the goal of the change, mitigated by unreachable protected/governance classes, consent-gated write, single-note audited revertable writes, and the optional narrowing allowlist); the governance fence being a denylist rather than an exhaustive list; the case-sensitive `_NEVER_FILES` edge; and the absence of app-layer rate limiting on `/register`, `/authorize`, `/consent` (accepted as an edge/funnel concern). Out of scope are a malicious operator, multi-tenant authorization, and dependency supply chain.

The write-guard and auth surfaces are CODEOWNERS-routed to the maintainer (`serialize.py`, `frontmatter_gate.py`, `commit_note.py`, `audit_log.py`, `auth.py`, `auth_cloud.py`, `mcp_server.py`, plus `SECURITY.md`, the threat model, the license/public-scan scripts, and `.github/`), changes to them must cite `SECURITY.md` and the threat model, and the repository's doc-drift table requires the write-guard docs (SECURITY.md, the threat model, the write-path section of ARCHITECTURE.md, the write-model pins in docs/README.md, the write-guard bullet in AGENTS.md, README.md's 'How it works') to move in the same PR — the same rule applies to auth/serving changes touching `auth*.py` / `mcp_server.py`.

Security problems are reported privately (email or GitHub private vulnerability reporting), never as a public issue; a report must not contain live tokens, hostnames, or addresses; and only the latest released version is supported, with no backports.

Current serving topology as it bounds writes: one public OAuth `/mcp` endpoint carries every remote client (read tools always, the gated `commit_note` write tool by scope) alongside a tailnet read companion on `:8848` that is read-only and auth-off, while the `:8849` client-credentials AS lane is retired — so a write boundary described as 'tailnet-only' is superseded.
